text:
Minnesota has points in 14 straight (11-0-3), and the only blemish on the last week was a shootout in Vancouver on Saturday in which the Wild went 0 for 3, Kirill Kaprizov hitting the post. Kaprizov has his own 14-game point streak, 28 points in it, and Matt Boldy has goals in three straight. The Wild have 39 points and a 99% playoff chance in our numbers, and they take 56% of the expected goals (expected goals measure the quality of chances).

The worry is the man who had been matching Kaprizov stride for stride. Quinn Hughes, 34 points in 24 games this season, left a game against Calgary after a collision and is on injured reserve until about Nov. 27. In the one game without him, Brock Faber played more than 29 minutes beside Jonas Brodin. In goal, The Athletic's Michael Russo reported that Filip Gustavsson makes his season debut, which is why tonight's numbers carry no projected Wild starter. Minnesota's goaltending as a whole has been 16.3 goals better than expected, the biggest reason a +35 goal difference outruns +18.8 on chances. Danila Yurov, per Russo, can finally exhale after months of trade rumors.

San Jose is playing better than its chances again, 3-1-1 in its last five while taking 45% of the five-on-five expected goals, and Saturday's 4-3 win over Seattle came with a Macklin Celebrini one-timer that made the highlight shows. Rookie Ivar Stenberg has moved up beside Celebrini and Will Smith with Igor Chernyshov out, and is playing 20 minutes a night. Dmitry Orlov, 11 points in his last ten, is one assist from 300. Jacob Trouba is out at least a week and Kiefer Sherwood is on injured reserve. Yaroslav Askarov starts at .888 and 3.8 goals saved above expected, a big turn from last season's -19.4.

The Wild beat San Jose 4-1 on Nov. 6, and our numbers make them the stronger side again, 3.92 expected goals to 2.86.
headline: Wild bring a 14-game point streak to San Jose
